notes: Day 1 baseline - dev slice, 5-trial pass@1. No mechanism. Dual-control stalling accounts for ~40% of failures.
Act IV mechanism run - explicit action policy engine (agent/policy.py). Dual-control stall rate reduced from ~40% to ~18% of failures. pass@1 +8.0 pp vs baseline, +4.7 pp vs published reference.
First real live run - keyword detection too narrow (word-order mismatches causing false negatives). Fixed in harness v2. Use next run for accurate baseline.

ablation_description: Policy layer active with full escalation rules; confidence gate REMOVED — all classified known intents trigger autonomous action regardless of confidence score.
notes: 10-task subset (dev_task_001–010), 5 trials. Removing confidence gate reduced stalling on low-confidence cases but introduced false-positive autonomous actions. pass@1 matched reference (42%) but worse precision than full mechanism — low-confidence POSITIVE emails sent autonomously when human review was correct.

ablation_description: Confidence gate active at 0.65; hard-coded escalation rules REMOVED — budget objections, NDA requests, GDPR questions, UNSUBSCRIBE eligible for autonomous action if confidence >= 0.65.
notes: 10-task subset (dev_task_001–010), 5 trials. Routine cases identical to full mechanism. The dev subset contains few explicit escalation tasks, so pass@1 appears similar to full mechanism. Production impact would be severe: budget and legal escalation cases handled autonomously without management review. Benchmark does not capture this compliance failure mode.
